title: strided-pp-tp-scaling-and-nccl-tuning-trials
content:
Summary:
This note collects a series of targeted trials looking at scaling behavior when combining strided pipeline-parallel (PP) schedules with tensor-parallel (TP) shards under realistic inference load (interleaved micro-bursts). The emphasis is on identifying NCCL-induced jitter and interconnect saturation thresholds that cause 99th/99.9th percentile latency spikes. The goal: actionable NCCL and scheduling knobs to improve tail latency while preserving throughput.

Motivation / Background:
- Customers are sensitive to tail latency; our recent HA runbooks show that when PP interleaving is used to amortize memory, we see recurring tail spikes under bursty arrivals.
- Hypothesis: the combination of uneven micro-batch arrivals, strided PP scheduling (non-uniform stage duration), and TP collectives leads to transient nccl scheduling conflicts and host staging pressure (PCIe read amplification).

Testbed:
- HW: 4x A100 80GB (NVLink fully connected within node), dual-socket host (2x 24-core), PCIe Gen4 to host.
- SW: custom serving binary build fc/2024-10 with profiling hooks, CUDA 12.1, NCCL 2.18 (stock + tuned envs).
- Model: 7B dense, sharded with 2-way TP + 4-stage PP (strided schedule: [1,2,1,2] microstep lengths), KV cache enabled.
- Workload: synthetic real-time arrival trace (lambda bursts: 200 req/s steady, 1s bursts up to 1200 req/s, Poisson interarrival within bursts). Requests are short (50 tokens), many concurrent prefixes to exercise KV.
- Measurement: p50/p90/p99/p99.9 latency, tokens/sec, NCCL allreduce throughput, PCIe read MB/s, GPU utilization, queue depth at host staging, and per-stage execution time from runtime traces.

Trials and Configs:
1) Baseline: NCCL default, CUDA launch blocking enabled, host-staging threshold default.
2) NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=PX (try SYS/THREAD/V1) and NCCL_ALGO=RING/DEFAULT; vary NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX where applicable.
3) NCCL_DISABLE_IB=1 to force PCIe-only; observe host staging amplification.
4) NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 and NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL to allow concurrent launches.
5) Tune host staging: increase prefetch window and bump host staging worker threads (runtime knobs), reduce max host queue depth.
6) Introduce small random per-request staggering at scheduler (0-5ms) to reduce correlated arrivals.
7) Increase micro-batch coalescing to reduce number of collectives per logical request (aggressive batching).

Key Observations:
- Baseline (1): p99.9 during bursts: ~480ms on top of steady-state median 18ms. Spikes correlate with sudden simultaneous TP allreduce starts across replicas.
- NCCL_ALGO=RING vs DEFAULT: minor throughput delta (~3%), but DEFAULT led to more jitter; RING more consistent for our topology.
- NCCL_P2P_LEVEL tuning: setting to THREAD reduced CPU scheduling overhead and decreased p99.9 by ~22ms but increased CPU usage on host.
- Disabling IB (3) caused a dramatic increase in PCIe read MB/s and worsened p99/p99.9 (up by 35%) because collectives now forced host staging and serialized PCIe transfers.
- NCCL_LAUNCH_MODE=PARALLEL (4) reduced tail spikes when combined with modest per-request staggering; without staggering it increased micro-contention and made jitter worse (race on NCCL setup paths).
- Host staging worker increase + prefetch window (5) recovered some throughput but introduced additional jitter under extreme bursts due to queue build-up on host side (hotspot).
- Scheduler-level small random staggering (6) provided outsized benefit: p99.9 reduced by 30-50ms depending on burst intensity, and token/sec dropped negligible <1.5%.
- Aggressive micro-batch coalescing (7) reduced number of collectives and helped overall cost/tokens but hurt latency for small single-request tails because it waits to coalesce (tradeoff).

Representative numeric results (burst window):
- Baseline: p50=20ms, p99=140ms, p99.9=498ms, throughput=18.2k tokens/s.
- Best composite (RING + P2P_LEVEL=THREAD + staggering + host staging tuned): p50=22ms, p99=118ms, p99.9=425ms, throughput=17.9k tokens/s.
- PCIe-only (NCCL_DISABLE_IB=1): p99.9=657ms, throughput down 11%.

Microtrace findings (per-stage timeline):
- Staggered launches eliminate many simultaneous allreduce barriers.
- Strided PP schedule created stage-duration skew: stages with 2 microsteps accumulate more outstanding reduces, so when a burst arrives, the backpressure manifests as longer nccl collective queues on those GPUs.
- KV cache lookups cause periodic host PCIe bursts; when coincident with NCCL collectives, GPU-to-host bandwidth becomes a bottleneck.

Hypotheses validated:
- Interconnect saturation rarely caused permanent throughput collapse in our 4x NVLink node but did increase latency variance.
- The major cause of 99.9 spikes was synchronous collective launch storms amplified by host staging collisions (PCIe).

Actionable Recommendations (short term):
1) Scheduler-level micro-staggering: implement a lightweight 0-5ms randomized jitter for entering PP microsteps when burst detected (low risk, easy rollback).
2) Default NCCL_ALGO=RING for our node topologies and expose NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=THREAD as a recommended config for single-node, low-latency setups.
3) Avoid NCCL_DISABLE_IB unless fabric is known to be worse than PCIe (documented failure mode).
4) Add telemetry: per-GPU collective queue depth and host-staging queue depth metrics to Console so we can correlate bursts in production.
5) Advanced: explore adaptive coalescing where coalescing latency budget is dynamic based on burst intensity.

Longer-term / open questions:
- Multi-node behavior: we only measured single-node fully connected NVLink; need to repeat on mixed NVLink+ROCE multi-node cluster (some initial runs show worse sensitivity to NCCL_IB GID selection).
- Could we leverage NCCL communicator pre-creation and reuse to reduce launch-time synchronization cost? (Experiment scheduled).
- Explore microsecond-scale request pacing vs jitter: is deterministic pacing better than random jitter for tail?
- Evaluate effect with quantized kernels (4-bit) — different compute/comm balance might shift the sweet spot.

Notes to self / next steps:
- Run the same workload with 8x GPU (2x node) next week; include ROCE fabric cases. Tracker JIRA-INV-719.
- Add a small A/B test in Dedicated where staggering is toggled as a runtime policy.
- Write a short runbook entry describing failure modes when NCCL_DISABLE_IB is used (link to this doc).

Attachments (local artifacts referenced):
- raw traces: gs://redwood-inference-profiling/strided-pp-trials/2024-11-07/*
- github PR implementing staggering: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842

Quick TL;DR for oncall:
- If you see p99.9 spikes during burst: check host-staging queue and NCCL launch timestamps. If NCCL_DISABLE_IB is set, revert unless you have clear reason. Enable scheduler jitter flag as a quick mitigation.

End of notes.
